speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand what is happening during these episodes, could you describe exactly how long they last and what you observe immediately before and after they occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste suggests an aura, pointing toward focal aware seizures evolving into impaired awareness. Do you have any history of head trauma, high fever, or other neurological issues in your family?

speaker: Doctor
text: That post-ictal confusion is a classic sign of a seizure, confirming my suspicion. To pinpoint the origin of these focal seizures, I need to see the electrical activity of his brain during or between episodes. REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG findings of right temporal lobe spikes strongly correlate with the patient's olfactory aura and focal impaired awareness seizures, confirming a diagnosis of focal epilepsy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
